title: Our attempt at creating an AI trading bot
author: _foursix_
selftext:
We started experimenting with AI trading capability in April and built a bot to run using a centralized swarm strategy. The theory is that AI should not just be better at trading than a human, but actually *very good* at trading. Early testing was full of pitfalls, but through self-healing, the AI was able to create what seems to be a profitable AI trading brain, not as an algo, but as a skilled, smart, and aware trader that doesn't get emotional. What that means is as the AI bot trades or manages a portfolio, inefficiencies and mistakes are addressed and improved by the AI coding model under direction. Gates, rules, and prompt engineering is improved vastly over time as it trades through different market regimes. Over-fitting is mitigated by keeping a level of openness and unpredictability, fully market aware, while ensuring it can never do something bad/hallucinatory. The brain (which we named Melli) is now at 10.5k lines of highly tuned code, with the whole swarm package at 40k.   
At the same time, LLM models continue to get better and more powerful, this in-turn has allowed much faster and smarter self-healing. For example gates and calculations are devised to filter out market noise and to rank legitimate instruments for trading (i.e. liquid enough, POP, reasonable spread widths, trending up, signals, etc.) since AI cannot process large amounts of data fast as a hard coded algo can, but AI can *use* algos.

Melli is as market-aware as anything I've seen out there so for in the AI trading domain, whether FOMC minutes coming up, ERs, the hormuz strait, etc., and she makes decisions with this awareness. We've tested Gemini and GPT models, optimized AI usage on the swarm (a complex model is not necessary scouting sentiments, for example), and continue to improve it. If you want to try it,see [www.swarmtrade.online](http://www.swarmtrade.online)
